files.lesson.md: --- order: 18 unit: binomials node: AC9M9A02 n4 uses: [AC9M9A02 n1, AC9M9A02 n2, AC9M9A02 n3] assumes: [AC9M9A01 n1, AC9M9A01 n2, AC9M9A01 n3] # x × x = x² only connection: ball-arc title: Expand or factorise? summary: "Expanding and factorising undo each other. Factorised form shows where the curve meets zero; expanded form shows where it starts." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "The same curve, written two ways. Each way answers a different question." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8343 url: http://127.0.0.1:8343/index.html readySelector: "#sl-p" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: curve.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$y = (x - 2)(x - 3)$ meets the x-axis at 2 and 3, because each bracket is zero there." } explainClip: query: { code: "@curve.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Factorised form shows where the curve meets zero" say: "Match the curve. Each bracket is zero where the curve meets the axis." clip: - caption: { text: "The dashed curve is x² − 5x + 6.", say: "The dashed curve is x squared minus five x plus six." } - click: Make p bigger - click: Make p bigger - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "Move p and q until the curves match: p = 2, q = 3.", say: "Move p and q until the curves match." } - click: Make q smaller - click: Make q smaller - click: Make q smaller - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "(x − 2)(x − 3): zero at 2 and at 3.", say: "Two and three: each bracket is zero there." } - wait: 900 --- You've expanded two brackets and factorised back. Now: when do you want each form? ## Predict: which form? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a form before the board shows who thinks the expanded form says where the curve meets the ground, and who sees that a bracket equal to zero does." check: type: predict q: "A skate bowl's floor is the curve $h = x^2 - 6x + 5 = (x - 1)(x - 5)$, with $h$ the height above the ground line in metres. Which form tells you most quickly where the curve meets the ground line?" options: - "$(x - 1)(x - 5)$" - "$x^2 - 6x + 5$" - "Both tell you at a glance" - "Neither: you need a graph" actual: "(x − 1)(x − 5). The curve meets the ground line where h = 0. A product is zero when one bracket is zero: x = 1 or x = 5. The expanded form shows h = 5 at x = 0 instead." ``` The floor of a skate bowl dips below the ground line. Where does it meet the line? ## Run: match the curve ```step stage: run insight: "Moving p and q until the curve matches shows that the numbers in the brackets are where the curve meets the axis." try: { playground: board, starter: "curve.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Move $p$ and $q$ until the solid curve covers the dashed one. Where does it meet the axis? Was your prediction right?", when: "p = 1 and q = 5" } ``` The dashed curve is $y = x^2 - 6x + 5$. The solid one is $y = (x - p)(x - q)$. Match them, and look at where the points sit. ## Investigate: two forms, two questions ```step stage: investigate insight: "Factorised form shows where the curve meets zero; expanded form shows the start value. Leo expands to check but doesn't compare every term." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Factorise $x^2 - 7x + 10$. Type $x^2$ as x^2." answer: "(x - 2)(x - 5)" form: factorised feedback: - ["(x + 2)(x + 5)", "That makes +7x. The middle is −7x."] explain: "−2 and −5 multiply to 10 and add to −7." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#leo" text: "Leo factorises $x^2 + x - 6$ and checks by expanding. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 5 fault: logic misconception: check-not-compared explain: "Line 5: the expansion gives x² − x − 6, not x² + x − 6. The middle terms differ, so it isn't a match. The numbers should add to +1: −2 and 3, so (x − 2)(x + 3)." - check: type: question q: "The curve is $y = (x - 2)(x - 5)$. Where does it meet the x-axis?" options: ["At 2 and at 5", "At −2 and at −5", "At 10 only", "At −7"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Each bracket is zero at the opposite sign: x − 2 = 0 means x = 2.", "10 is where it meets the y-axis (2 × 5 = 10), not the x-axis.", "−7 is the middle number of the expanded form: it isn't a meeting point."] explain: "x − 2 = 0 at x = 2 and x − 5 = 0 at x = 5." ``` ### Undo it Here's moving from expanded to factorised, and what each form shows. ```worked x^2 - 6x + 5 :: Start: expanded. -1 \times -5 = 5, \; -1 + -5 = -6 :: Two numbers: multiply to 5, add to −6. (x - 1)(x - 5) :: Factorised. x - 1 = 0 \text{ or } x - 5 = 0 :: A product is zero when a bracket is zero. x = 1 \text{ or } x = 5 :: Where the curve meets the axis. \text{start: } 0^2 - 6 \times 0 + 5 = 5 :: From the expanded form: where it meets the y-axis. ``` Now try one on paper: $x^2 - 8x + 12$. Where does the curve meet the axis, and where does it start? Then type the smaller meeting point. ### Find the mistake Read Leo's working. Compare every term. ### What the curve says ## Modify: move the curve ```step stage: modify insight: "Moving p and q shows factorised form giving the meeting points straight away, while the start value needs the expanded form (p × q). One meeting point makes a bracket squared." try: { playground: board, starter: "curve.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: ["Set p to 2 and q to 6.", "The points sit where the curve meets the axis."] check: { type: number, q: "The curve is $y = (x - 2)(x - 6)$. Where does it meet the x-axis on the left?", answer: 2, explain: "x − 2 = 0 at x = 2. The other point is x = 6." } - hint: ["Put x = 0 into the expanded form.", "$(0 - 2)(0 - 6)$ is the same thing."] check: { type: number, q: "Where does $y = (x - 2)(x - 6)$ meet the y-axis? That's its value at $x = 0$.", answer: 12, explain: "(0 − 2)(0 − 6) = (−2)(−6) = 12. In the expanded form x² − 8x + 12 it's the last number." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the last step: what's $-2 \\times (-6)$?", answer: 12, explain: "A negative times a negative is positive: 12." } - hint: ["Set p and q to the same number.", "Where do the points go?"] check: { type: number, q: "Edge case: how many times does $y = (x - 3)^2$ meet the x-axis?", answer: 1, explain: "(x − 3)(x − 3): both brackets are zero at x = 3. The curve touches the axis once, then goes back up." } ``` ### Where it meets the axis ### Where it starts ### One meeting point ## Practise: move between the forms ```step stage: practise insight: "Moving in both directions, mixed, and saying what each form shows; the review keeps expanding fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x - 4)(x + 9)$." answer: "x^2 + 5x - 36" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 - 5x - 36", "The numbers are −4 and +9: they add to +5."] explain: "−4 + 9 = 5 and −4 × 9 = −36." - check: type: answer q: "Factorise $x^2 + 4x - 21$." answer: "(x - 3)(x + 7)" form: factorised feedback: - ["(x + 3)(x - 7)", "That makes −4x. The bigger number is positive."] explain: "−3 and 7 multiply to −21 and add to 4." - check: type: question q: "You want to know where the curve $y = x^2 - 3x - 10$ meets the x-axis. What do you do first?" options: ["Factorise it to (x − 5)(x + 2)", "Put x = 0 into it", "Expand it"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That gives where it meets the y-axis: −10.", "It's already expanded."] explain: "Factorised form shows where each bracket is zero: x = 5 and x = −2." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Which two numbers multiply to −10 and add to −3? Type the negative one.", answer: -5, explain: "−5 and 2 multiply to −10 and add to −3." } - check: type: answer q: "Review: expand $(x - 6)(x - 6)$." answer: "x^2 - 12x + 36" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 36", "There are two strips of −6x: −12x."] explain: "−6 + (−6) = −12 and (−6)(−6) = 36." ``` ### Expand ### Factorise ### Choose a form ### Review A bracket squared, from Two brackets. ## Make: back to the skate bowl ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the opening: the factorised form gives where the bowl meets the ground line, and the expanded form gives the height at the start." tasks: - hint: ["Find two numbers that multiply to 5 and add to −6.", "−1 and −5."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The bowl is $h = x^2 - 6x + 5$. Where does the floor meet the ground line, and how high is the edge at $x = 0$? Give the smaller meeting point." steps: - ["$x^2 - 6x + 5 = (x - 1)(x - 5)$", "factorise: −1 and −5 multiply to 5, add to −6"] - ["$x = 1$ or $x = 5$", "each bracket is zero"] - ["$h = 5$ at $x = 0$", "put x = 0 into the expanded form"] answer: "1" answerLabel: "Smaller meeting point" feedback: - ["5", "5 is the height at x = 0. The meeting points are where h = 0."] - ["-1", "x − 1 = 0 means x = 1."] criteria: - "I factorised before reading off the meeting points." - "I used the expanded form for the height at x = 0." - "Both my meeting points make a bracket zero." explain: "(x − 1)(x − 5) is zero at x = 1 and x = 5. At x = 0 the height is 5." - check: type: question q: "Which statement is true of $y = (x - 1)(x - 5)$ and $y = x^2 - 6x + 5$?" options: ["They are the same curve", "They are different curves with the same start", "They cross the x-axis at different points"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Expanding the first gives the second exactly.", "Both meet the axis at 1 and 5: expanding doesn't move the curve."] explain: "Expanding and factorising rewrite the same curve. Only the form changes." ``` ### The bowl Back to the skate bowl. Work it out on paper first, then type the smaller meeting point. ### Same curve **Also used in** - **Thrown balls.** A ball's height follows a curve like this one, upside down. Its landing time is where the curve meets the ground line. - **Next.** Solving quadratic equations: making a product equal zero. ```teacher summary: "Students see expanding and factorising as undoing each other, match a curve y = (x − p)(x − q) to an expanded one on a graph, and use each form for what it shows: meeting points or start value (AC9M9A02, node 4)." time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can expand and factorise to move between the two forms. - I can read where a curve meets the x-axis from the factorised form. - I can find where it starts from the expanded form. struggle: "Choosing which form to use. Ask students what the question wants: where it meets the axis (factorise) or where it starts (the last number)." before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Factorising quadratics and The pattern. Graphing parabolas is not assumed: the board just shows a curve and where it meets the axis. The one idea: the two forms are the same curve. Factorised shows where it meets zero; expanded shows where it starts (the last number). The common mistake is checking an expansion without comparing every term (Leo's working). running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose the expanded form can't yet say why a product being zero helps." - "Run: ask students to say each point's coordinates before moving on." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the bowl in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for both forms side by side." - "Modify: before (x − 3)², ask how many meeting points they expect." stuck: - see: A student says (x − 2)(x − 5) meets the axis at −2 and −5. ask: What x makes x − 2 equal zero? fix: "x = 2: the sign flips from the bracket." - see: A student says the curve starts at the middle number. ask: What's y when x = 0? fix: "Put x = 0 in: the last number." stretch: What does x² + 4 look like? Can you factorise it? Use the graph. support: "A two-column table: factorised form on the left, expanded on the right, with the meeting points and the start value to fill in." leads: > Continues AC9M9A02 node 4. Where it leads: solving quadratic equations, and parabolas and their turning points (Year 10). exit: q: Where does y = (x + 4)(x − 7) meet the x-axis? a: At x = −4 and x = 7. explain: > Expanding and factorising are opposites. $(x - 1)(x - 5)$ and $x^2 - 6x + 5$ are the same curve. Factorised form shows where it meets the x-axis: each bracket is zero, at $x = 1$ and $x = 5$. Expanded form shows where it starts: put $x = 0$ in to get 5. ```

# Boards for "Expand or factorise". The dashed curve is y = x² − 6x + 5; the solid one is (x − p)(x − q).

# region: run

y: -6, 10
grid: 1

point B: q, 0

files.working.txt:
# Leo's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: leo
Factorise x² + x − 6.
Two numbers that multiply to −6: 2 and −3.
So x² + x − 6 = (x + 2)(x − 3).
Check: (x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − 3x + 2x − 6 = x² − x − 6.
That matches, so it's right.
# endregion
